title: Unveiling the mechanism of calcitriol in treating type 2 diabetes mellitus: A combined network pharmacology and in vitro approach targeting ERS-related pathways.
authors: Zeng, Fanqiang; Liao, Yimei; Jiang, Jianping; Zhao, Chengjian; Peng, Shuihua; Zhang, Huijie; Zou, Hui; Tan, Shudan; Qiao, Liya; Liu, Fan; Huo, Juan; Yan, Zhigang; Xu, Yongli
one_liner_zh: 该文用网络药理学和分子对接研究骨化三醇治疗2型糖尿病的ERS相关通路，虽含分子对接但核心是药物-蛋白靶点而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) has emerged as a major global public health concern, characterized by increasing prevalence and serious complications that contribute substantially to societal healthcare costs. Concurrently, endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS) has been increasingly appreciated as a central pathogenic mechanism underpinning the development and progression of T2DM. Calcitriol has been shown to have a beneficial effect in the treatment of T2DM. However, the therapeutic targets and potential mechanisms of calcitriol against T2DM through modulated ERS-related pathways remain poorly understood. To systematically investigate these mechanisms, we adopted an integrated approach combining network pharmacology, molecular docking and experimental validation. Initial network pharmacology analysis identified STAT3, HSP90AA1, MAPK1, and PIK3R1 as potential key targets mediating calcitriol's anti-T2DM effects. These computational predictions were then experimentally validated using a high glucose (HG)-induced MIN6 cell model. Functional assessments using CCK-8 assays and flow cytometry demonstrated that calcitriol improved the survival of pancreatic beta-cells and reduced glucose-induced cell death. Moreover, the results from real-time fluorescent quantitative PCR and western blot analysis revealed that calcitriol reversed the HG induced upregulation of STAT3, HSP90AA1, MAPK1 and PIK3R1 mRNA and protein levels in MIN6 cells. The findings from our study may offer insights into the underlying mechanisms through which calcitriol exerts its therapeutic effects on T2DM by targeting potential ERS-related pathways.
abstract_zh: 2型糖尿病（T2DM）已成为全球重大公共卫生问题，其特点为患病率不断上升及严重并发症，显著增加了社会医疗成本。同时，内质网应激（ERS）日益被认为是驱动T2DM发生与发展的核心病理机制。骨化三醇已被证明对T2DM治疗具有有益作用。然而，骨化三醇通过调节ERS相关通路对抗T2DM的治疗靶点及潜在机制仍知之甚少。为系统探究这些机制，我们采用了一种整合网络药理学、分子对接和实验验证的综合方法。初步网络药理学分析确定STAT3、HSP90AA1、MAPK1和PIK3R1为介导骨化三醇抗T2DM效应的潜在关键靶点。随后，利用高糖（HG）诱导的MIN6细胞模型对这些计算预测进行了实验验证。使用CCK-8实验和流式细胞术的功能评估表明，骨化三醇改善了胰腺β细胞的存活率，并减少了葡萄糖诱导的细胞死亡。此外，实时荧光定量PCR和Western blot分析结果显示，骨化三醇逆转了HG诱导的MIN6细胞中STAT3、HSP90AA1、MAPK1和PIK3R1 mRNA及蛋白水平的上调。我们的研究结果可能为骨化三醇通过靶向潜在ERS相关通路发挥其对T2DM治疗作用的潜在机制提供见解。
